**Starter questions (Amber)**  
Give me quick answers so we can build a safe messaging feature:

1. Who will use this app? (Just you, a small team, the public, etc.)  
2. On day 1, what 3 things must it do?  
3. What private data will you keep? (email, phone, message text, etc.)  
4. Will people need to log in (email‑only magic link, etc.)?  
5. Is there any money involved (paid plans, paid chat features, etc.)?  
6. What stack are you using? (Bolt + Supabase – you said that, but do you already have a Supabase project set up? Any existing tables? )

**Safety parts I’ll build in (always for a messaging feature in Bolt + Supabase)**

| Feature | Safety part |
|---------|-------------|
| **Private messages** | 1️⃣ Supabase row‑level‑security (RLS) on the `messages` table so users can only read/write their own rows. 2️⃣ Limit message size (e.g., 2000 chars) and block plain‑text URLs or disallowed content. 3️⃣ Add a “report” flag per message that admins can review. |
| **Logins with email only (magic link)** | 1️⃣ Use Supabase Auth’s magic‑link flow. 2️⃣ Set your site address in Auth settings and enable “Redirect URLs” for Bolt. 3️⃣ Connect an e‑mail provider (e.g., SendGrid) so your own credentials handle sends. |
| **Data privacy** | 1️⃣ All message content stays in the Supabase bucket/database, never exposed on the client. 2️⃣ If users delete their account, we’ll soft‑delete their messages and bucket files and anonymise any personal data. |
| **Key safety** | 1️⃣ Store the Supabase service key in Bolt’s Secrets panel, never in the client code. 2️⃣ Add a spending cap on the Supabase API usage (by setting a daily function quota if you exceed). |
| **Backup & recovery** | 1️⃣ Enable Supabase’s automated backups for your database. 2️⃣ Create a “save point” before adding the new table. |

---

```
What we are building: a private messaging section in a Bolt app.  
Who uses it: …   Risk level: Amber (logins, personal messages).  
Day‑one features: 1. Users sign up/ log in via magic link. 2. User can send a message to another user. 3. User can view their inbox.  
Information it stores: message text, sender/recipient IDs, timestamps (private – only each user sees their own messages).  
Logins: email‑only magic link (Supabase Auth).  Money: none.  
Built with: Bolt (no-code front‑end) + Supabase (backend/database).  
Steps: 1. Create Supabase project / tables. 2. Configure Bolt‑Supabase connector. 3. Add login widget. 4. Add message form & list. 5. Add RLS policies. 6. Test with two test accounts. 7. Commit to production.  
Safety: keys secret, data locked to owner, RLS enforced, save point before each step.  
Not in v1: file uploads, admin dashboard, paid plans.  
```
